origins: Struggles with reading, math, attention, or processing can bring years of corrections, low grades, and comparisons. Labels like “slow” or “lazy” stick, and many carry the word “dumb” into adulthood.
teaches: “God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.” “Not many of you were wise by human standards.” Peter and John were “unschooled, ordinary men” whose boldness amazed people because “they had been with Jesus” (Acts 4:13). God gives each person different gifts, and “to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.” Learning differences are real, and they say nothing about your worth or your intelligence in other areas.
errors: Believing I am either smart or dumb.
Predicting that I will always fail.
Feeling slow and concluding I am dumb.
questions: Who first called me dumb, and what did they know about me?
What does Scripture say about God’s choices?
truth: I am not dumb. I learn differently, I have gifts, and God uses people of all abilities. I can find the help and methods that fit me.
hw_truths: God chose the weak and foolish things.
Ordinary people with Jesus do remarkable things.
I have gifts for the common good.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
log: Each week, note one strength used and one help sought.
actions: Write ten things you do well.
Try listening, pictures, or hands-on work.
Say it when you feel dumb.
prayer: Lord, I have been called dumb for so long. Show me my gifts, lead me to help that fits, and heal old wounds. Amen.
hw_questions: Who first called me dumb, and what did they know about me?
What does Scripture say about God’s choices?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God chose the weak things of the world.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I'm dumb.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
